definition: Optimal (v,k,1) CPCW code (equivalently optimal (v,k,1) OOC): s=floor((v-1)/(k(k-1))) k-subsets (codewords) of Z_v whose k(k-1)s ordered differences are nonzero and pairwise distinct; for even v the difference v/2 is then necessarily absent. Definition and optimality bound as in the source; parent must re-read them before accepting any candidate.

primary_attestation.source: Baicheva, Topalova, On the Existence of Optimal (v,5,1) and (v,6,1) Binary Cyclically Permutable Constant-Weight Codes, Axioms 15(1) (2026) 35, DOI 10.3390/axioms15010035
primary_attestation.quote: The question marks mean that we could not find optimal codes for these values of v and the question of the existence of such codes remains open. In particular, we have not found examples of optimal (v, 5, 1) CPCW codes for v = 143, 144, 146, 162, and 167, and of optimal (v, 6, 1) CPCW codes for v = 122, 123, 124, and 126.

acceptance.existence_per_case: Strict-format code file with SHA-256; prep verifier ACCEPT; a parent-written independent checker ACCEPT; seed/command replay by the parent; mutation controls. Each v is a separate finite claim.
acceptance.nonexistence_per_case: Only with a complete written proof (counting/necessary-condition argument checked by parent and hostile review) or a certified exhaustive classification: two independent implementations with stated symmetry reductions, each proved sound, plus positive controls rediscovering known optimal codes (e.g. 121/125/126 for k=6) and exact counts on smaller published classifications. UNKNOWN, timeout, heuristic failure or a single unaudited exhaustive run is not nonexistence.
acceptance.gate: Any single case constructed and fully verified closes a stated open case; all eight decided would complete the frozen list.

search_guidance: Start with k=6 (only 4 codewords; exhaustive classification may be feasible with translation and multiplier normalization). Then k=5 with structured ansätze (multiplier-invariant base blocks, relative difference family forms for 162, prescribed leaves) and complete local search. Freeze each representation in README before running. Preserve every negative run with its exact scope.
